wiki_text: Venture Global declared commercial operations at Calcasieu Pass on April 15, 2025, reaching its commercial operation date (COD) approximately 68 months after the August 2019 final investment decision. The declaration followed a prolonged commissioning period and a dispute with foundational offtakers (who alleged Venture Global sold commissioning cargoes on the spot market rather than under their long-term SPAs while the plant remained in 'commissioning'). LNG had first been produced in January 2022. FERC had authorized placing the remainder of the facilities (power island, pre-treatment, LNG storage, boil-off-gas and marine facilities) in service.

In August 2025, Kimmeridge closed a strategic equity investment from Mubadala Energy and rebranded its integrated natural-gas platform - combining its upstream operations (formerly Kimmeridge Texas Gas, now Caturus Energy) and Commonwealth LNG - as 'Caturus.' Mubadala Energy holds a 24.1% equity stake in the Caturus platform and CPP Investments raised its platform stake to ~31% (contributing ~$1.2 billion). On May 15, 2026, Caturus (with Mubadala Energy, Kimmeridge and CPP Investments) announced a positive final investment decision on the 9.5 mtpa Commonwealth LNG export facility in Cameron Parish, Louisiana, closing $9.75 billion in project financing (within ~$21.25 billion total commitments). Commercial operations are targeted for 2030. NOTE: Mubadala's investor entity here is Mubadala Energy, distinct from 'Mubadala Investment Company PJSC' currently in GEM's Parent field; the Mubadala/CPP stakes are described at the Caturus platform level.

topic: Phase 1 / Phase 2 FIDs and construction progress (2025-2026)
wiki_text: Venture Global took FID and closed $15.1 billion in project financing for CP2 Phase 1 (with the associated CP Express Pipeline) on August 6, 2025 - at the time the largest standalone project financing in the U.S. bank market. CP2 had received DOE non-FTA export authorization on March 19, 2025 and a FERC Final Supplemental EIS on May 9, 2025. On March 13, 2026, Venture Global took FID and closed an additional $8.6 billion financing for CP2 Phase 2, bringing total CP2 financing to ~$20.7 billion. As of early 2026, construction was on budget and on track for first LNG in the second half of 2027 (two of four storage tanks had roofs raised; 12 of 36 trains on foundations).

Sempra Infrastructure and partners TotalEnergies, Mitsui & Co and Japan LNG Investment continued to advance the proposed Cameron LNG Train 4 (~6.75 mtpa). FID, repeatedly targeted for H1/mid-2025, was not taken in 2025. In November 2025 FERC granted a five-year extension to commence construction of the one-train expansion. The DOE non-FTA export authorization for the expansion was noted as expiring May 2026, prompting potential extension requests. A competitive EPC process (Bechtel and others) was under way to de-risk cost. The Cameron 'Debottlenecking (T1-T3)' uprate concept (~0.68 mtpa) is recorded in GEM as cancelled (2026).

topic: FERC pre-filing and Baker Hughes technology selection (2025)
wiki_text: Argent LNG entered the FERC pre-filing process (approved October 2025) for its proposed Port Fourchon, Louisiana export terminal (up to ~25 mtpa, structured as Phase 1 ~12 mtpa and full buildout to ~25 mtpa). Argent selected Baker Hughes as the liquefaction technology and equipment provider (NMBL modularized solution powered by LM9000 gas turbines; commitment to five LM9000 units reported Sept 2025) - Baker Hughes is a technology vendor, not an equity owner. An early ~5 mtpa long-term offtake heads-of-terms with Bangladesh was reported. Sponsor materials target Phase-1 construction in 2026 and commercial operations by 2030.

Delfin Midstream advanced its deepwater FLNG project (up to 13.2 mtpa across up to three floating LNG vessels) toward FID. Samsung Heavy Industries won the exclusive EPCI contract for the first FLNG vessel (Oct 2025), and in January 2026 Delfin extended the SHI letter of award and executed a Siemens Energy purchase order, with FID expected 'in the next month.' On April 22, 2026, Expand Energy signed a 20-year offtake SPA with Delfin FLNG 1 LLC, expressly subject to FID. As of the research window FID had not been formally taken; first commercial operations are targeted for the second half of 2030.
